fixes.why: no needs_humans line, so the tags come from the work: an open bot people write (#coding) and a game-playing model trained on gpu time people can lend (#compute). #ai and #games are already on the card.

blender track builders and texture artists model the apollo 17 terrain and its textures (#3d-modeling) and turn it into a raceable three-lap track (#level-design). no #playtesting: the done test is ai karts finishing.

needs_humans names three crowds: pixel artists for blocks, guns and monsters (#pixel-art), mappers to rebuild nine maps (#level-design), and playtesters who feel a bad hitbox (#playtesting). the 60 fps engine work is code (#coding).

mariano's case. hardware and firmware designers (#electronics), people who run production and ship across borders (#manufacturing), hosts in quake-prone places (#hosting) in at least 20 countries (#worldwide), seismologists to tune detection (#research with the field tag #seismology), and people who have lived through quakes and can say what a shake felt like (#lived-experience). this is the vocabulary's own example; #needs-humans stays, first.
people draw their own neighborhood by hand (#drawing) in at least 5 countries (#worldwide), and anyone who knows their street can draw one (#beginner-friendly). #art stays as the topic tag.

people in at least 20 countries (#worldwide) each record one minute of outdoor sound (#recording) with a phone (#phone), which takes no special skill (#beginner-friendly). birders who check species get the free tag #birding beside the topic tag #birds. model builders are already #ai.
an astronomer catches false signals from thruster firings and flares (#research; the field tag #astronomy is already there), and the result is an open notebook working from raw pixels (#coding).

people across many latitudes on both sides of the equator (#worldwide), with a stick and a phone photo (#phone) and no special skill (#beginner-friendly). the card's #anyone-can-join turns into #beginner-friendly in the cleanup, so the card doesn't show both.

needs_humans asks for an eye for tile families, which #math already covers. the hunt is a polyform search people write and run (#coding) on spare cpu time (#compute), the same as the other math searches.

the work is writing an explanation a person can follow (#writing, #teaching). #math and #lean cover reading the paper. the cold reader who tries the explanation needs only measure theory and some probability, which #math covers.

needs_humans asks for someone who can tell which constant is ripe (#research; the field is #math, already there) and a write-up a referee can follow (#writing). the bounds fall to a computer search plus a checker script (#coding).

no needs_humans line, so the tags come from the work: a model pull request that cuts the error (#ai, #coding) without leaking data from after forecast time (#data). the card's #ml folds into #ai in the cleanup.
people who read a grid operator's site in its local language (#many-languages) and know where its public data lives (#locals); each zone is a parser (#coding, beside the card's #python).
no needs_humans line, so the tags come from the work: joining epa's result files to service-area outlines and listing unmatched systems (#data), for us water systems (#usa). #maps is already there.

no needs_humans line, so the tags come from the work: turning the usda snap store file into county-by-year counts (#data) for every us county (#usa). table work like this is #data on every card, not #coding.
careful listeners fix every caption line (#transcription), in whatever language each clip uses (#many-languages). no #video: nobody shoots or edits video here.

two checkers compare 100 random rows against the stories (#proofreading), and the output is an open table of places, coordinates and quotes (#data). fans who know the canon well enough to tell doyle's made-up places from real ones find it by the free tag #sherlock-holmes, the way fans tag on instagram.
screen reader users judge the spoken math (#screen-reader), and each pull request is code merged into latexml (#coding). latex experts who know rare packages get the free tool tag #latex.

kernel and rust developers, authors for each base tool and arch packagers who build the image are all #coding (#rust is already there; packagers are #coding on arch core too), and people who boot it and report what breaks are #testing.
screen reader users who tell a useful label from a useless one (#screen-reader); each fix is a few lines merged through gerrit (#coding). #needs-humans stays, first.

each of the 100 games is played through by 2 people (#playtesting), and ruffle fixes in rust are merged upstream (#coding; #rust is already there). people who remember flash games or keep old collections find it by the free tag #flash.

doom players of any skill record pistol-start demos on maps they haven't played (#playtesting, and #beginner-friendly because fresh players are the point), and mappers fix broken spots in freedoom's style (#level-design).

can't pass without 10 blind and low-vision players on different screen readers (#screen-reader), who design and play it through (#playtesting); the mod and helper app are code, and luanti takes only human-written code (#coding).
#pixel-art is already there for the artists. the 20 people who take the quiz cold need no skill at all (#beginner-friendly).
needs_humans names two people: someone who keeps moss alive and damp for weeks (#gardening) and someone who solders a micropower circuit (#electronics).

95 people each draw one glyph with a pen or a mouse (#drawing), with no font skill needed because agents do spacing and builds (#beginner-friendly). #art stays as the topic tag. no #design: agents handle the type design.
every song needs 2 proofreaders who check it note for note against the scan (#proofreading). reading and engraving sheet music is #music, already on the card.
people with an eye for drawing in characters (#drawing). #art and #ascii stay as topic tags. nothing else is needed: checkers only match scenes to photos.

someone who keeps plants alive (#gardening), and the wheeled pot with light sensors and matching loggers (#electronics), the same pair as the moss-powered clock. 'people with sunny rooms' has no tag; #gardening is the closest.
every report is coded into a table by two people (#data), and experienced epidemiologists settle tricky coding calls (#research, beside the field tag #epidemiology).

air-quality people who know which monitors in their country are reference grade (#research; the field tag #air-quality is already there). the work pairs sensor and station tables (#data) into an open correction model a second person reruns (#coding).

people from the papers' fields judge whether a changed output is a real difference or noise (#research; the field tag #biomedical is already there), and fixing broken jupyter notebooks is #coding. no #compute: the runs are small.
gravitational-wave people pick priors and spot bad runs (#research; the field tag #gravitational-waves is already there), and the runs and configs are python (#coding). #compute is already there.
reading each lean statement line by line against its source (#proofreading), and knowing what erdős meant from the original papers (#research; the field is #math). #lean is already there.
#math, #lean, #mathlib and #geometry already say who this needs: lean users with taste in definitions, and reviewers on the lean zulip. no new tag needed.

people who read the source papers and judge whether a replay is really independent (#research; the field is #math), and each replay is code with logs (#coding). no #compute: the card names no big runs.
pattern spotting that leads to a new public decider is #coding. #math, #compute and #rocq (the proofs) are already on the card.

people with an oven, a kitchen scale and their own soil (#cooking), each wiring a sensor to a board to read it (#electronics), and a soil scientist to review the method (#research; the field tag #soil is already there).

many mappers and osm validators (#maps; the card's #mapping folds into it in the cleanup), in madagascar (#madagascar), and mappers there who know where lines really run (#locals). #openstreetmap is already there.

owners of monitored heat pumps dig out their own design facts (#lived-experience), installers and heat pump designers judge which inputs are known before install (#research; the field tag is #heat-pumps after the cleanup), and the open table and model are #data.

30 open parametric parts are designed in cad (#3d-modeling), then printed and fitted by people with 3d printers (#3d-printing; the card's #3dprinting folds into it in the cleanup). repair cafe volunteers are #repair, already there.
repairers who read a two-line fault note are #repair, already there; native speakers for the non-english rows (#many-languages); labeling fault types in a table (#data).
residents confirm their own city's totals (#locals), people who know a general fund from a capital fund pull spending out of budget books (#data), for every us city over 100,000 people (#usa).

volunteers phone or email utilities (#outreach), ideally people who live in each system's area (#locals), plus people who read an inventory file and pull out the counts (#data), for us water systems (#usa).
riders in each city take sampled trips door to door and log the time (#fieldwork), in the 10 biggest us cities (#usa), plus people who run the routing pipeline (#coding).

people in all five boroughs (#locals; #nyc and #fieldwork are already there) walk to a restroom and take a photo with a phone (#phone); noting whether it was open and step-free takes no special skill (#beginner-friendly).

parents, teachers and students keep a sensor running at their school for a month (#hosting; #schools is already there), flagging schools means joining federal files (#data), and it covers us public schools (#usa).
people who write clear alt text (#writing) and screen reader users to judge it (#screen-reader). #alt-text is already there.

fluent sicilian speakers (#sicilian) finish the interface strings (#translation), approve sentences and validate clips (#proofreading), and at least 50 speakers record (#recording). same tags as the tagalog card.

lots of volunteers confirm fuzzy matches one at a time, which takes care, not a special skill (#beginner-friendly); matching a 79,554-row catalog is #data. wikidata editors who know bot approval are covered by #wikidata.

braille readers of each language approve its table, so the language tags are how they find the card (#braille and #nigeria are already there); teachers at nigerian schools for the blind are #teaching. the card's text says 'nigeria's three biggest languages' without naming them.

wikipedia editors read each source and write each edit (#writing), and people who know a field judge whether a source backs the claim (#research). librarians with journal database access have no tag; see gaps.
many patient ears write down what is sung (#transcription) and spot-check each other's work (#proofreading). #music is already there.

players who know wesnoth's campaigns, on different browsers and devices, finish each one twice and spot units or the ai acting wrong (#playtesting); compiling to webassembly is #coding (#porting is already there).
arch users try the old steps on real hardware a vm can't fake, like laptops and gpus (#testing), then fix the wiki page (#writing).
people with their own machines run independent rebuilds (#compute), and packagers get fixes accepted upstream and in arch's packaging repos (#coding).
native bengali speakers (#bengali; #translation is already there) who know some python (#python, a free tool tag), and one person to be the translation coordinator python asks for (#organizing).
audio and video people who can tell whether a filter's output is right (#audio; #video and #testing are already there); the tests are merged upstream (#coding).

pixel artists (#pixel-art), chiptune composers (#music; #chiptune stays beside it), and people who play it start to finish on a real game boy with a flash cart (#playtesting). owners find it by #game-boy, which the card's #gameboy folds into in the cleanup.
game designers tune hunger and night length (#design) by playing until it feels tense, not tedious (#playtesting); the hunger meter and spawn rules are mod code (#coding).
game theorists who know chain and loop strategy prune the search (#research, with the free field tag #game-theory), and the solver is code (#coding). #compute is already there.

singers of any level (#singing, #beginner-friendly), each recorded alone on a phone (#recording), and someone to mix 100 voices (#audio). arranging is #music, already there. the card's #choir folds into #singing in the cleanup.

knitters by machine or by hand (#crafts; #knitting stays beside it) in 20 places, each knitting their own place's climate (#worldwide). owners of a brother machine with an ayab board are covered by #knitting.

people who 3d print, assemble and test in batches (#manufacturing; #3d-printing is already there), optics people who cut cost without losing resolution (#research with the free field tag #optics), and schools, clinics and small labs (#schools) in 5 countries (#worldwide) who take one and use it.

people in at least 10 countries (#worldwide) build a two-camera rig (#diy) and shoot the hidden test set (#photography); people who know astrometry solve the reference photos (#research with the field tag #astronomy). model builders are already #ai.

social scientists who read a regression table and judge whether a rerun matches the paper (#research; the field tag #social-science is already there); getting 2,000 r files running is #coding (#r is already there).

20 volunteers who only wear electrodes for ten minutes (#beginner-friendly), someone with eeg experience to judge signal quality (#research; the field tag #neuroscience is already there), and the board and electrodes put together at home (#diy).

microscopists who read tb smears label every photo (#research; the field tag #microscopy is already there), from labs in at least 5 countries (#worldwide); the benchmark tests detectors (#ai). no #photography: the labs share photos they take for their own work.

reviewers who read research combinatorics and number theory and catch a statement that is subtly too weak or too strong (#research, with the free field tag #number-theory beside #additive-combinatorics). #lean is already there.

people who write oeis entries editors accept (#writing), a second reader for each of the 248 (#proofreading), and terms computed for many sequences (#coding; #compute is already there).
